records.name: Strawberry Mansion Community Development Corporation
records.summary: A Strawberry Mansion neighborhood nonprofit that works on housing repair, historic preservation, and resident programs. It hosts free family events, such as a spring movie night at The Yard.
records.what_you_do: Come to free community events, sign up for the newsletter, or fill out the Volunteer with Us form on the site to ask how to help with the group's housing and land care work.

schedule.text: Free community events are announced on the group's events page as they come up. No weekly or monthly schedule is published.

first_step.how: Fill out the Volunteer with Us form on the group's volunteer page, or email info@strawberrymansioncdc.org to ask how to help. Watch the events page for the next free event and come along.
first_step.basis: Free events are open to the public, and the volunteer form and an email address give a clear way in. The site describes no newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events are free and family friendly, such as an outdoor movie night. The site does not describe what a volunteer shift looks like, so send an email first to ask what the work involves.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page for the next date before you go
Email the office with questions about volunteer work before you come

records.notes: The events page lists an October 8 monthly meeting and an October 18 potluck with no year, and a 2024 footer. The weekdays match 2020, so those listings were not used as evidence. Status rests on the May 2026 movie night. The volunteer form is the only join route found, and no volunteer dates are published. The site gives no accessibility or language information.

records.name: Taller Puertorriqueño
records.summary: A Puerto Rican arts and culture center in North Philadelphia that shows art, runs youth and family art programs, and keeps an archive on Puerto Rican history in the city.
records.what_you_do: Enroll in the weekday after-school Cultural Exploration Program for K to 8 students, a summer camp, or the Young Artist Program. Adults can come to a tour or hands-on workshop, see an exhibition or public talk, or become a member.

schedule.text: The after-school Cultural Exploration Program runs Monday to Friday, 3 to 6 pm, for K to 8 students. Exhibitions and public events run on dated listings on the events page.

cost.text: The after-school program is free, with a one-time $30 registration fee that also covers summer camp registration. Tours, workshops and exhibitions list no prices on the site.

access.notes: The after-school page says the building is wheelchair accessible, with wide ramps, wide doorways and accessible bathroom stalls. The site is in Spanish and English. For accommodations, call 215.426.3311.

first_step.how: New after-school students fill out the CEP English Application on the after-school page, or returning families email mrodriguez@tallerpr.org. Adults can call 215.426.3311 or come to the next public event.
first_step.basis: The after-school page sets out a clear first step for new students, and public events list how to get tickets or an RSVP. The site also welcomes visitors to tours and the bookstore.
first_step.what_to_expect: Students in the after-school program spend weekday afternoons from 3 to 6 pm in cultural exploration activities, after a one-time $30 registration. Public exhibitions and talks are open to visitors, and some events ask for an RSVP. The bookstore and archive are on site.
first_visit_tips: Call 215.426.3311 before you visit to ask about accommodations
Check the events page for RSVP dates on panels and talks
The bookstore and archive are on site, so you can come just to look around

records.notes: The Young Artist Program and Summer Camp pages were not read in full, so their days, ages and prices are not recorded. The after-school page says enrollment is open for a program starting October 5, 2026. The after-school staff contact is named on the page and was not recorded as a contact.

records.name: Tenant Union Representative Network (TURN)
records.summary: A Philadelphia tenant group that teaches renters their rights, runs eviction and repair clinics, and helps tenants form tenant unions in their buildings. It also staffs help lines for renters.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a free one-hour tenant rights webinar, in person or on Zoom, call the hotline for counseling, attend a repair or eviction defense clinic, or join the Network as a renter who organizes with neighbors.

schedule.text: Free tenant rights webinars run several times a week, Monday to Saturday, in person or on Zoom. Sign up in advance for a time that works for you.

cost.text: The webinars and hotline counseling are free. Landlord inspections and background checks cost a fee.

first_step.how: Register for a webinar by calling 267-635-4130 or using the Zoom registration link on the webinars page. For urgent help, call the hotline at 267-635-4100 and press 3.
first_step.basis: The webinars are designed to educate tenants, each one ends with questions to an attorney or housing counselor, and the site gives a phone line and a join page with clear steps.
first_step.what_to_expect: A webinar lasts about one hour, in person or on Zoom, and covers tenant rights in rental housing. It ends with a question and answer period with an attorney or housing counselor. The sessions give general information, not legal advice.
first_visit_tips: Register ahead by phone or online
Write down your question about your own lease or repair issue for the question period
If you do not have internet access, call 267-635-4130 and staff will sign you up

records.notes: The webinar times were read from a list of links, so confirm exact days and times by phone. The register page lists an email address that looks unrelated to TURN, so it was not recorded. The site's dated news runs 2022 to 2024. The status rests on the June 2026 Temple listing and on the current webinar and hotline pages.

records.name: The People's Fridge
records.summary: A West Philadelphia food group that runs free pop-up food giveaways and a warehouse that rescues and passes along groceries to community fridges.
records.what_you_do: Get free groceries at the Saturday pop-up on the 2nd and 4th Saturdays, or ask the group how to help with food rescue and distribution.

schedule.text: Free pop-ups on the 2nd and 4th Saturdays of the month, 2 to 4 pm.

first_step.how: Come to the Cedar Park pop-up at 50th and Baltimore on a 2nd or 4th Saturday between 2 and 4 pm. To ask about volunteering, email hello@thepeoplesfridge.org or use the Contact form on the site.
first_step.basis: The pop-ups are free and open to neighbors, and the site gives an email address and a contact form. The site does not describe the visit in detail, so the rating stays at 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: Pop-ups are short Saturday afternoon giveaways of free food at the corner of 50th and Baltimore. The site does not say what to bring or whether you need ID, so ask before your first visit.
first_visit_tips: Email hello@thepeoplesfridge.org before your first visit to ask about ID or what to bring
Other Saturdays have no pop-up, so come on a 2nd or 4th Saturday

records.notes: The site lists no phone number and names no volunteer roles or sign-up rules. It says volunteer events are planned and can be raised by email or the form. Ask before the first visit about ID and what to bring. The summary and schedule are carried from tier 1 with the site's current pop-up schedule.

records.name: Philadelphia Canoe Club
records.summary: A paddling club founded in 1905 that teaches canoeing, kayaking and stand-up paddleboarding from its boathouse on Ridge Avenue. It runs trips, training and social paddles through the year.
records.what_you_do: Take a lesson, join an open club event or trip, or come to a work day at the boathouse. Club trips, training and events do not require membership.

schedule.text: Club meetings are held monthly on the third Monday evening at 7:30 pm. Lessons, trips and work days run through the year, and the calendar lists them by date.

cost.text: Full membership is a $25 application fee plus annual dues up to $180. Club trips, training and events open to the public do not need membership, and trip and lesson fees were not published on the pages read.

first_step.how: Come to Fall Work Day #1 on Saturday, October 10, 2026 at 9:30 am at 4900 Ridge Ave, or email admin@philacanoe.org to ask about lessons and open paddles.
first_step.basis: The site says trips, training and events are open to the public and do not need membership. Lessons range from recreational kayak and paddleboard to whitewater and pool sessions, so there is a path for beginners.
first_step.what_to_expect: Work days and open events happen at the boathouse on Ridge Avenue. The site does not say how long a lesson runs or what it costs, so ask by email before you sign up for one.
first_visit_tips: Park along the driveway if there is room, or follow the Additional Parking signs
A SEPTA bus stop sits at the driveway entrance on Ridge Ave, at the traffic light
Email admin@philacanoe.org to ask about lesson times and prices before you come

records.notes: The club is also known in IRS records as The Wissahickon Mills Foundation. The lessons and classes pages returned 404, so lesson lengths, ages and prices were not found. The site's dated items run from October 2026 into January 2027, including club meetings on October 19 and November 16 and a Fall Work Day on October 10.

records.name: Thursday Night Contra Dance (PATMAD)
records.summary: A weekly contra dance in Mount Airy run by the nonprofit Philadelphia Area Traditional Music and Dance group, with a beginner lesson before each dance.
records.what_you_do: Take the beginner lesson at 7:30 pm, then dance from 8 to 10:30 pm. Admission is pay what you wish.

schedule.text: Every Thursday: beginner lesson at 7:30 pm, dancing from 8 to 10:30 pm. The caller and band change from week to week, and there is no dance on Thanksgiving week.

locations.label: The Irish Center (Commodore John Barry Arts and Cultural Center), ballroom entrance

cost.text: Pay what you wish, with a suggested $10, $15 or $20 or more.

first_step.how: Arrive by 7:30 pm at the ballroom entrance, the one furthest from Carpenter Ave, for the beginner lesson before the dance starts at 8.
first_step.basis: A beginner lesson starts before every dance, admission is pay what you wish, and the site tells you which entrance to use and says safety volunteers are at events.
first_step.what_to_expect: The beginner lesson runs at 7:30 pm, then the dance goes from 8 to 10:30 pm. Admission is pay what you wish with a suggested $10, $15 or $20. The site says snacks to share are welcome, with no peanuts or peanut butter, and masks are optional.
first_visit_tips: Arrive by 7:30 pm for the beginner lesson
Bring finger foods to share, with no peanuts or peanut butter
Look for the signs and use the ballroom entrance furthest from Carpenter Ave
Check the site's directions page for parking before you go

records.notes: The site lists dance dates without a year. The 2026 year is inferred from the page's references to 2026 events. The about and FAQ pages returned 404. Separate guest-caller events listed on the site, such as Center City and Ardmore dances, were not recorded as this group's events.

records.name: University City Hospitality Coalition
records.summary: A volunteer-run group that serves free hot meals and sandwiches to people in West Philadelphia's University City, with church and campus partners hosting the meals. It also works to ease hunger and homelessness in the neighborhood.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer at a partner church dinner by setting tables, serving plates, or cleaning up, help assemble take-out meals, or donate food or money. Email volunteers@uchcphiladelphia.org to sign up.

schedule.text: Hot dinners are served at partner churches and campus sites on several weeknights at about 6 pm, with a Saturday midday meal on one listing. Volunteer shifts run about 5:30 to 7:15 pm. Confirm the schedule before going.

first_step.how: Email volunteers@uchcphiladelphia.org to sign up for a meal shift, arriving around 5:30 pm. You can also call (856) 209-3819 to confirm the schedule before a shift.
first_step.basis: Volunteer shifts have a clear email route and a set routine, and the site explains the basic tasks. The site does not describe how a first shift is set up, so the rating stays at 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: A shift runs about 1 hour 45 minutes, from about 5:30 to 7:15 pm. Volunteers set tables, portion food, serve plates and tea, assemble take-out meals, and clean up after dinner. The site asks volunteers to wear gloves, tie back long hair, and stay home if they are sick.
first_visit_tips: Arrive around 5:30 pm, since cleanup ends about 7:15 pm
Wear gloves if you can and tie back long hair
Do not come if you are sick
Volunteers under 18 must come with a parent or legal guardian

records.notes: The meal information page returned 404, so meal sites and days come from an undated PA 211 listing, which says to confirm before going. The group's own site lists (856) 209-3819, while the earlier listing showed (610) 639-4395; the site number is recorded. The site's mailing address is a post office box and was not recorded as a location. Groups cannot volunteer at meals, but they can run donation drives. The site lists no dated volunteer days.

notes: Seven groups deep-read with 20 fetches and no WebSearch calls. Several site pages returned 404 (Contra Dance about and FAQ, Canoe lessons and classes, UCHC meal information) and were skipped, not treated as blocks. The Strawberry Mansion events page has undated listings whose weekdays match 2020, so they were not used as evidence. Budget left: 2 WebSearch and about 40 fetches, not used.
